rv.q: Driven by authenticity, earnestness, youth and ample heart, “The Outsiders” is very much an outsider itself.

But, scenic designers AMP and Tatiana Kahvegian’s tactile set of crunching dirt, exposed scaffolding and tire towers captures more authentic grit than any of the pugnacious characters do.

The production is the platonic ideal of a retro classic rebooted for Broadway, broadly appealing to audiences young and old (my showing was split between boomers and kids) but not particularly searing, recognizable but not terribly distinct, sincere and competent yet not resounding.
I suspect that a lot of people will like The Outsiders more than I did.
